Voice-Controlled Robotic Platform

Explore AICORE's completed voice-controlled robotic prototype combining spoken-command recognition, command mapping, embedded control, and motor actuation.

A working robotic platform controlled through supported spoken commands, combining voice recognition, command interpretation, embedded control, and motor actuation.

Objective: Demonstrate voice-driven human-robot interaction for controlling a mobile robotic platform.

System overview: A supported spoken command is recognized and mapped to a defined action. The embedded controller then sends the corresponding actuation command to the robotic platform.

Status: Completed Prototype. A working technical prototype implemented and demonstrated by AICORE. It is presented as engineering evidence, not as a production-certified commercial robot.

AICORE contribution: Voice-command definition, Voice-recognition integration, Command interpretation and mapping, Embedded controller integration, Motor actuation, Prototype testing.

Capabilities demonstrated: Supported spoken-command recognition, Voice-to-action command mapping, Embedded control, Motor actuation, Mobile-platform control, Human-robot interaction prototyping.

Technologies and system elements: Voice recognition, Command-processing logic, Embedded control, Motor-drive electronics.

Demonstrated results: The completed prototype recognized its supported spoken commands. Recognized commands were translated into corresponding robotic movement actions.

Limitations: The platform is not described as unrestricted conversational or natural-language control. Recognition accuracy, supported languages, environmental noise tolerance, and production reliability are not claimed.
